claim_text: The accepted partition assigns Castle Defense to the Action and defense cohort.
The accepted identity ledger uses sentence/castle-defense as Castle Defense's canonical identity.
interpretation: The source identity is sentence-based while the catalog id is castle-defense.

claim_text: The identity ledger records catalog identity id castle-defense for canonical identity sentence/castle-defense.
interpretation: Separates catalog id from route identity.

claim_text: The phase-3 identity reconciliation records sentence/castle-defense as current, non-blocking, and matched.
The advantage-games catalog registers id castle-defense with title Castle Defense, sentence route href, and playable status.
The advantage-games catalog's Castle Defense cover is /games/cover/castle-defense-cover.png.
The accepted identity ledger records the advantage-games and reading-advantage sentence page aliases for Castle Defense.
interpretation: Both host page copies are accepted aliases.

claim_text: The accepted identity ledger records the canonical route /student/games/sentence/castle-defense for the advantage-games host.
The accepted identity ledger records the reading-advantage route /apps/reading-advantage/app/student/games/sentence/castle-defense as a host copy.
No accepted source-denominator record uses a vocabulary/castle-defense page, component, logic, or API path; the accepted source records use sentence/castle-defense paths.
interpretation: Full-file machine check; legacy vocabulary assets are recorded separately in the asset denominator.

claim_text: The advantage-games sentence page dynamically imports CastleDefenseGame from the sentence/castle-defense barrel with SSR disabled.
The reading-advantage sentence page dynamically imports CastleDefenseGame from the sentence/castle-defense barrel with SSR disabled.
The advantage-games completion route exports POST from createCompleteRoute and is force-static.
The advantage-games sentences route exports GET from createSentencesRoute(SAMPLE_SENTENCES) and is force-static.
The reading-advantage completion route protects and logs requests before dispatching CastleDefenseController.completeGame.
The reading-advantage ranking route protects and logs requests before dispatching CastleDefenseController.getRanking.
The reading-advantage sentences route protects and logs requests before dispatching CastleDefenseController.getSentences.
The advantage-games page fetches /api/v1/games/castle-defense/sentences with the current locale.
The advantage-games page POSTs xpEarned, difficulty, accuracy, correctAnswers, and totalAttempts to /api/v1/games/castle-defense/complete after completion.
The accepted source denominator contains the advantage-games and reading-advantage Castle Defense sentence page, completion, sentence, and ranking route records.
interpretation: Full-file machine check of route records.

claim_text: The canonical component configures RankingDialog to request /api/v1/games/castle-defense/ranking.
The accepted source denominator contains no advantage-games Castle Defense ranking route file at the frozen baseline.
interpretation: Full-file machine-checked route absence; reading-advantage has a ranking route.

claim_text: The scene-state denominator records CastleDefenseGame at the advantage-games sentence page.
The scene-state denominator records CastleDefenseGame at the advantage-games sentence component.
The scene-state denominator records CastleDefenseGame at the reading-advantage sentence page.
The scene-state denominator records CastleDefenseGame at the reading-advantage sentence component.
The canonical game state status union contains playing, gameover, and victory.
interpretation: Complete state field inventory includes no pause status.

claim_text: The canonical game state stores player, enemies, towers, tower slots, projectiles, words, base, path, wave, sentence, and collection counters.
The canonical component renders a loading state before image assets are ready.
The canonical component renders GameStartScreen while hasStarted is false.
The canonical start scene exposes three localized instructions and move, build, and collect control hints.
The canonical start scene exposes easy, medium, and hard difficulty buttons and a leaderboard button.
The active scene renders a React-Konva Stage and Layer when game state and dimensions are available.
The canonical results scene renders GameEndScreen for both gameover and victory states.
The canonical results scene reports score, XP, accuracy, waves cleared, and enemies defeated, and uses onRestart to return to the menu.
The canonical component has no pause or resume state, handler, or rendered pause control in its full baseline source.
The reading-advantage component state accepts easy, normal, hard, and extreme difficulty values and defaults to normal.
The game world is 800 by 600 pixels with 50-pixel tiles, a player radius of 20, and player speed 3.
Soldiers have radius 12, HP 40, and speed 0.8; tanks have radius 18, HP 120, and speed 0.7; bosses have radius 25, HP 360, and speed 0.6.
interpretation: All enemy strength and movement variants.

claim_text: Towers have range 150, fire every 1000 milliseconds, and deal damage 10; projectiles have radius 5 and speed 8.
The base starts at HP 100 with radius 40; the tick is 50 milliseconds, spawn rate is 2000 milliseconds, and the active enemy cap is 15.

Waves 1 through 6 contain respectively 10 soldiers; 8 soldiers and 4 tanks; 10 soldiers, 5 tanks, and 1 boss; 12 soldiers, 8 tanks, and 1 boss; 15 soldiers, 10 tanks, and 2 bosses; and 20 soldiers, 12 tanks, and 3 bosses.
The default enemy path is a U-shaped waypoint path from (75,75) through (75,525) and (725,525) to (725,75).
The six map configurations provide wave-specific paths, tower slots, and base positions.
interpretation: All six terrain and defense-zone variants.

claim_text: Road tile selection returns EW for horizontal path segments, NS for vertical segments, and CORNER with a direction-derived rotation at corners.
Initial state starts in playing status at wave 1 with no enemies, towers, or projectiles, a random sentence, an empty collection, and a randomized 12-by-16 grass map.
Canonical difficulty changes base HP to 150 for easy and 80 for hard while medium retains base HP 100.
The player movement reducer normalizes diagonal input, scales by delta time, and clamps the player within the world bounds.
Wave-configured spawning emits soldiers before tanks and bosses, assigning each type its corresponding HP, speed, radius, and waypoint index zero.
Without an explicit wave configuration, boss spawning is available from wave 5 below random roll 0.1, tank spawning from wave 2 below random roll 0.3, and soldier is the default.
interpretation: Legacy random strength variant retained in the logic module.

claim_text: Enemies move toward their current waypoint and advance the waypoint index when within five pixels of it.
Circle collision uses the sum of radii and inRange uses squared distance against squared range.
Sentence parsing trims input, splits on whitespace, strips non-alphanumeric edge punctuation, and removes empty words.
interpretation: Typed-answer content is represented as sentence words rather than a text-input answer field.

claim_text: Canonical XP uses correct and incorrect collection counts, with bonuses for perfect accuracy, at least half base HP, under 120000 milliseconds, and at least three completed waves, capped at 10.
A word collection is valid only when its index equals the number of already collected words and is not already collected.
Sentence words spawn as Word records in the middle 50 percent of the board, with sentence indices in order.
interpretation: Word target field and sentence ordering.

claim_text: Collecting a valid word marks it collected and adds its translation to player inventory; an invalid word sets invalidCollection without marking that word collected.
An invalid collection resets inventory, collected indices, sentenceCompleted, and respawns the current sentence words.
A tower can be built only when sentenceCompleted is true, the player is within 50 pixels of an empty tower slot, and the slot has no existing tower.
Building a tower creates an active tower with range 150 and damage 10, clears inventory and sentence progress, and spawns a different next sentence when available.
The legacy checkTowerActivation function requires the player to be near an empty slot and carry the slot targetWord before creating a tower.
interpretation: This exported helper is distinct from the sentenceCompleted flow used by the main tick.

claim_text: Active towers fire only after their cooldown and target the closest enemy within tower range.
Projectiles move toward their target, apply projectile damage on collision, are removed after a hit or dead target, and dead enemies are filtered out.
Enemies reaching the end of the path are removed and damage the base by 30 for a boss, 15 for a tank, and 10 for a soldier.

The main tick updates time and player movement, collects words, handles resets and tower construction, moves enemies, applies base damage, updates towers and projectiles, scores kills, and marks sentence completion.
The main tick spawns only until the current wave quota is reached and requires both the spawn interval and the maximum-enemy cap to pass.
Completing a non-final wave waits through a two-second wave message, loads the next map, clears towers and projectiles, and resets wave sentence and spawn counters.
Completing the final configured wave sets status to victory, clears the wave message, preserves final entities and score, and increments wavesCompleted.
interpretation: Terminal victory behavior; CD-MECH-005 establishes that the final configured wave is wave 6.

claim_text: The game sets status to gameover when base HP is zero or less.
The canonical game loop clamps frame delta to 50 milliseconds and advances the pure state tick with directional input and vocabulary.
interpretation: Runtime loop behavior at the canonical host.

claim_text: The reading-advantage game loop advances with useInterval at GAME_TICK_MS and calculates XP from score rather than the canonical state-based XP formula.
The reading-advantage logic accepts easy, normal, hard, and extreme difficulties and assigns extreme base HP 50.
The reading-advantage XP helper returns zero for non-positive score and otherwise returns the score multiplied by 0.01 rounded up.
The canonical state has no lives field and instead tracks base HP and maximum base HP.
interpretation: Health representation is base HP, not a separate lives counter.

claim_text: The canonical component contains no typed-answer text input, answer validator, or answer submission control in its full baseline source.
interpretation: Full component machine check; input is directional and collection-based.

claim_text: The canonical logic module contains no escort actor, escort objective, escort state field, or escort transition in its full baseline source.
The canonical entity types define soldier, tank, and boss enemies and no separate environmental hazard entity type.
interpretation: Enemy actors are the active hazards represented by the state model.

claim_text: The canonical component loads player_3x3_pose_sheet.png, goblin_3x3_pose_sheet.png, orc_3x3_pose_sheet.png, troll_3x3_pose_sheet.png, tower-base.png, tower-built.png, and player-castle.png from the sentence Castle Defense asset directory.
interpretation: Concrete actor, defense, and base asset paths.

claim_text: The reading-advantage component loads the same seven sentence Castle Defense asset paths.
BackgroundLayer loads grass_A.png, grass_B.png, grass_C.png, grass_D.png, road_EW.png, road_NS.png, and road_corner.png.
BackgroundLayer renders the selected grass tile and road tile at tile size, applying the road rotation returned by getRoadTileInfo.
Tower slots render tower-base.png with reduced opacity when occupied, while built towers render tower-built.png with a range ring.
The base renders player-castle.png at the current base position.
Soldier, tank, and boss enemies select goblin, orc, and troll sprite sheets respectively and render at sizes 40, 56, and 72.
interpretation: Enemy visual variants and strength-to-sprite mapping.

claim_text: Projectiles are rendered as yellow circles using the projectile state position and radius; no projectile image path is loaded by the canonical component.
Uncollected words are rendered as white circles with a black stroke and centered translation text.
The player sprite crop uses animation frames and switches row based on movement direction, flipping horizontally for leftward movement.
New towers create a green expanding build-effect circle that fades over 600 milliseconds.
Enemy health bars render a dark background and a green-or-red fill proportional to enemy HP.
The canonical catalog references cover/castle-defense-cover.png and the asset denominator records that cover as a baseline asset.
The asset denominator records the legacy reading-advantage vocabulary Castle Defense assets background.png, castles_3x2_sheet.png, and skeletons.png.
interpretation: Legacy vocabulary path is asset evidence, not canonical route evidence.

claim_text: The asset denominator records the current sentence Castle Defense assets under both advantage-games and reading-advantage hosts.
Phase 3 reconciles the advantage-games and reading-advantage BackgroundLayer files as a non-blocking matched copy pair.
The canonical Castle Defense component contains no audio asset path, audio element, or sound playback call in its full baseline source.
A successful page sentence fetch clears warningStatus and stores returned sentences; NO_SENTENCES and INSUFFICIENT_SENTENCES select warning states.
The canonical start handler creates state with the selected difficulty, sets hasStarted true, and enters fullscreen.
When game state reaches gameover or victory, the canonical loop computes accuracy, invokes onComplete with XP and difficulty, and exits fullscreen.
The page completion callback stores the last result before posting completion data.
The canonical back-to-menu handler clears hasStarted and gameState.
An invalid word collection invokes resetSentenceProgress in the main tick before later tower and wave processing.
A completed sentence sets sentenceCompleted true and adds 50 points exactly once for that completion.
A completed wave displays Wave N Complete for 2000 milliseconds before the next-wave transition.
The advantage-games page uses NO_SENTENCES as its loading-error fallback.
The reading-advantage host starts gameplay without calling enterFullscreen in its start handler.
interpretation: Host divergence from canonical fullscreen transition.

claim_text: The canonical loading, start, results, and active containers use full-width mobile sizing with md aspect-video fallbacks.
The canonical component observes container ResizeObserver contentRect and window resize and orientationchange events.
The canonical camera scale is the maximum of width scale, height scale, and 0.8, with camera coordinates clamped to world bounds.
interpretation: Compact and wide viewport camera behavior.

claim_text: The canonical Stage uses the measured container width and height and applies camera scale and translation to its Layer.
The canonical HUD uses a width capped by min(92vw,560px), mobile and md typography classes, and mobile bottom versus md top HUD positions.
The canonical virtual D-pad is positioned at bottom-right with pointer interaction enabled.
The canonical component consumes useAccessibilitySettings and retrieves getEffectiveTextSize for rendered text sizing.
interpretation: Shared accessibility settings are consumed by the canonical host.

claim_text: The reading-advantage component contains responsive width, aspect, and mobile/md position classes but does not import the canonical accessibility settings hook.
interpretation: Full-file host responsive and accessibility divergence check.

claim_text: No explicit matchMedia compact/wide branch or named compact/wide responsive contract occurs in the canonical component source.
interpretation: Full-file machine-checked absence; measured scaling is present but profile-specific behavior is not separately named.

claim_text: The canonical BackgroundLayer tests render the layer, wait for image-backed Konva images, and cover empty grass and empty path inputs.
The canonical component tests cover the initial start screen and transition to the Konva playing stage after Start is clicked.
The canonical component tests assert fullscreen entry, difficulty buttons, difficulty selection, and the default medium difficulty.
The canonical component tests assert the Konva layer, virtual D-pad, score HUD, and castle HP HUD during gameplay.
The canonical component test file includes a named completion callback test and renders the game through the active stage before asserting.
interpretation: The test does not force a terminal state; this limitation is visible in the cited assertion.

claim_text: The reading-advantage component tests cover the start screen, start transition, white word orbs, centered word text, Thai sentence HUD, progress and wave HUD, sentence-complete message, absent inventory HUD, and virtual D-pad.
The canonical logic tests cover sentence parsing, six map configurations, tower-slot placement, and wave configurations.
The canonical logic tests cover sequential word validation, collection, reset, sentence completion, tower eligibility, and tower construction.
The canonical logic tests cover performance counters, initial state sentence fields, XP bonuses and cap, movement, collision, and all three enemy spawn types.
The canonical logic tests cover tick movement, time, spawning, word persistence, base gameover, wave quotas, tank spawning, wave progression, final victory, and pre-final non-victory.
The canonical logic test asserts sentence completion awards points when all words are collected.
The reading-advantage logic tests cover the score-based XP helper, including zero score and ceiling behavior.
The original Castle Defense track describes a tower-defense game in which the player physically collects vocabulary words to build towers and defend a base.
The asset track describes integrating a tile-based background, roads, and game assets for Castle Defense.
The fixes track describes sentence loading, word collection mechanics, visual display, and fullscreen support fixes for Castle Defense.
The rewrite track records a complete rewrite using Wizard vs Zombie architecture patterns for mobile performance, with 30+ FPS achieved on mobile.
The start/end screens track requires a start screen, an end screen with score and XP, a restart button, and XP equal to ceil(totalScore * 0.01).
The compliance-audit spec identifies Castle Defense as a sentence game with a sentence component, castleDefense logic, sentence page, API, and sentence asset directory.
The compliance report records baseline coverage 49.47%, final coverage 80.45%, and a 25/25 passing result.
interpretation: Historical audit outcome; not a replacement for source evidence.

claim_text: The accepted historical-source denominator records both host Castle Defense page files as current classifications at the frozen baseline.
interpretation: Historical denominator reconciliation; no deleted Castle page record is present in the full-file search.

claim_text: The accepted historical-source denominator contains no Castle Defense record classified deleted; the full denominator search returns the two current page records only.
Phase 3 marks the Castle Defense identity reconciliation as non-blocking and matched, and the selected Castle asset reconciliations are also non-blocking and matched.
interpretation: Full-file machine check of selected phase-3 records.

claim_text: The accepted pilot manifest records zero denominator mismatches and zero unsupported factual claims in the predecessor pilot gate.
FIXTURE (must be REJECTED): Castle Defense grants a 2x XP multiplier on extreme-difficulty victories.
interpretation: Unsupported multiplier injection; canonical XP has no extreme tier and no 2x multiplier.

claim_text: FIXTURE (must be REJECTED): Castle Defense can be represented by a generic defense template with one enemy type, one map, and one tower because its source has no wave, sentence, or terrain variants.
interpretation: Contradicted by the six wave configurations and by the cited map, sentence, and enemy logic; generic-template substitution is not evidence.

claim_text: FIXTURE (must be REJECTED): Responsive behavior is proven solely by finding md: and h-[...] class keywords in the component.
interpretation: Keyword-only responsive inference omits ResizeObserver, measured dimensions, camera scaling, and compact/wide state evidence.
